text:
deploy-bot: automated deploy completed: wave=w-3307 at 2026-03-17T08:02:12Z. Canary traffic -> us-west1-runtime-canary

ashley_oncall: dashboards showing rising tail latency in canary slice, p99 up ~250ms. Also seeing increased paging and a spike in kernel_fallback metrics.

mike_runtime: link? suspect adaptive-batcher threshold change in this wave. if batcher grows too big it could thrash the kv cache and force kernel fallbacks.

jordan_sre: quick probe: `rate(kv.evictions[30s])` shows surge on 4 hosts. dumping relevant logs now.

jordan_sre (logs): ```
2026-03-17T08:03:10Z runtime[pod-17]: WARN adaptive-batcher: window=180ms queued=12
2026-03-17T08:03:11Z runtime[pod-17]: ERROR kernel_selector: fallback_to_generic op=matmul shapes=(1024,512)
2026-03-17T08:03:12Z runtime[pod-17]: WARN kvstore: eviction_ratio=0.92
```

tess_oncall: paging SRE now. This looks like potential customer impact for inference completions. Recommend immediate mitigation: flip feature flag `adaptive_batcher_enabled` -> false in us-west1.

incbot: incident elevated to P1 (SEV2) due to error rate and tail latency affecting customer SLAs. Notifying eng-sre + eng-runtime.

ashley_oncall: @tess_oncall please flip flag. @mike_runtime prepare rollback steps if flag flip isn't effective in 2min.

tess_oncall: executing: `rwdctl feature-flag set adaptive_batcher_enabled false --scope=region:us-west1`

tess_oncall: flag flip succeeded :white_check_mark: seeing p99 drop on 2 pods within 30s.

mike_runtime: good catch. keep monitoring. if kernel_fallback_count doesn't drop to baseline we'll run controlled rollback of wave w-3307: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime --to-revision=stable-3289 --namespace=runtime-prod`

jordan_sre: performing traffic backoff to reduce pressure while we observe: `rwdctl route update --service=runtime --split=canary=5,baseline=95 --wave=w-3307`

ashley_oncall: also note support queue: one high-touch enterprise reported slower completions in us-west1 (ticket #SUP-2019). tagging customer success.

ellie_csm: acknowledged. I'll draft internal comms and keep watch on customer thread. Hold public status until we confirm sustained recovery.

jordan_sre: metrics: kernel_fallback rate down ~70% after flag flip + traffic shift. paging metrics trending down.

tess_oncall: p50 back near normal. p99 still ~40ms above baseline but improving. throughput stable.

mike_runtime: I'll stay on the bridge for 30m to validate. Next steps: reproduce in preprod to confirm adaptive-batcher change is root cause and open PR to revert the batcher tuning. If rollback needed, I'll coordinate with releases.

ashley_oncall: agreed. leaving oncall handoff to @mike_runtime for monitoring and post-incident follow-up. I'll unassign now.

incbot: Incident state -> monitoring. Scheduled check-in: 20 minutes. Escalate if p99 > 200ms for >5% of requests for 10m.

ellie_csm: updating customer success with interim note: "We observed increased latencies for some requests in us-west1 after a canary update; mitigation in progress; monitoring closely."

tess_oncall: logs now show a small number of hosts still falling back on generic kernels for specific large-model ops. we'll run a targeted kernel-selector disable if those hosts don't recover.

mike_runtime: noted. I'll also run `make reproduce-adaptive-batcher` in sandbox to validate and add guardrails to the rollout script.

ashley_oncall: thanks team. last update 08:04:30Z — handoff complete to @mike_runtime. will reopen if regression reappears.
